## Analytical Blueprint for Airbnb New york

**Objective:** Uncover the core drivers of short-term rental profitability in th area of New York where there is a room for improvement.

## Description of the Data

1.  This data story explores the dataset of 14,253 bookable NYC Airbnb listings

2.  I examine the core structural, geographic, and operational factors that distinguish highly profitable listings from underperforming ones.

## Core Questions

1.  Which boroughs and neighborhoods yield best revenues?

2.  How do room types and pricing strategies influence occupancy rates?

3.  Where are the best opportunities for new property acquisition or operational optimization?

```{r load-libraries, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(leaflet)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(dplyr)
library(stats)


# Set global ggplot theme
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
            theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", size = 11),
                  panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

# Read datasets
listings <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Muhammad-Imran91/608/refs/heads/main/nyc_airbnb_listings.csv")
neighborhoods_sf <- st_read("neighbourhoods.geojson", quiet = TRUE)

# Calculate Daily Revenue and Occupancy Percentage if not directly provided
listings <- listings %>%
  mutate(
    daily_revenue = price * occupancy,
    occupancy_pct = occupancy * 100,
    host_is_superhost_label = ifelse(host_is_superhost == TRUE | host_is_superhost == "t", "Superhost", "Non-Superhost")
  )

```

```{r Market Revenue Baseline, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| fig-align: center


summary_stats <- listings %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Listings       = n(),
    Mean_Price           = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Price         = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Occupancy       = mean(occupancy_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Occupancy     = median(occupancy_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Daily_Revenue   = mean(daily_revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Daily_Revenue = median(daily_revenue, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# 2. Format labels and position cards into a balanced 2-Column Grid
kpi_data <- summary_stats %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "RawValue") %>%
  mutate(
    # Format values based on metric type
    ValueLabel = case_when(
      str_detect(Metric, "Price|Revenue") ~ dollar(RawValue, accuracy = 0.01),
      str_detect(Metric, "Occupancy")     ~ percent(RawValue / 100, accuracy = 0.1),
      TRUE                                ~ comma(RawValue)
    ),
    # Clean titles
    CleanTitle = case_when(
      Metric == "Total_Listings"       ~ "TOTAL MARKET VOLUME",
      Metric == "Mean_Price"           ~ "MEAN PRICE",
      Metric == "Median_Price"         ~ "MEDIAN PRICE",
      Metric == "Mean_Occupancy"       ~ "MEAN OCCUPANCY",
      Metric == "Median_Occupancy"     ~ "MEDIAN OCCUPANCY",
      Metric == "Mean_Daily_Revenue"   ~ "MEAN DAILY REVENUE",
      Metric == "Median_Daily_Revenue" ~ "MEDIAN DAILY REVENUE"
    ),
    # Color grouping by metric category
    Category = case_when(
      Metric == "Total_Listings"       ~ "Volume",
      str_detect(Metric, "Price")      ~ "Pricing",
      str_detect(Metric, "Occupancy")  ~ "Occupancy",
      str_detect(Metric, "Revenue")    ~ "Revenue"
    ),
    # 2-Column Grid Coordinates
    x = case_when(
      Metric == "Total_Listings"       ~ 1.5,
      str_detect(Metric, "Mean")       ~ 1.0,
      str_detect(Metric, "Median")     ~ 2.0
    ),
    y = case_when(
      Metric == "Total_Listings"       ~ 3.0,
      str_detect(Metric, "Price")      ~ 2.0,
      str_detect(Metric, "Occupancy")  ~ 1.0,
      str_detect(Metric, "Revenue")    ~ 0.0
    ),
    # Large, spacious box dimensions to fully enclose text
    tile_width  = if_else(Metric == "Total_Listings", 1.95, 0.95),
    tile_height = 0.82
  )

# 3. Plot Executive KPI Cards (2-Column Portrait Grid)
ggplot(kpi_data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  # Draw background card boxes with generous height and width
  geom_tile(aes(fill = Category, width = tile_width, height = tile_height), rx = 0.08, ry = 0.08, color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Metric Header Text (safely inside the upper half of the expanded box)
  geom_text(aes(label = CleanTitle), y = kpi_data$y + 0.18, fontface = "bold", color = "grey30", size = 2.7) +
  # Primary Value Text (safely inside the lower half of the expanded box)
  geom_text(aes(label = ValueLabel), y = kpi_data$y - 0.12, fontface = "bold", color = "grey10", size = 4.6) +
  # Scale and Color Styling (Fixed: using c() instead of [])
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Volume"    = "#f0f4f8",
    "Pricing"   = "#fef2f2",
    "Occupancy" = "#f0fdf4",
    "Revenue"   = "#faf5ff"
  )) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.4, 2.6)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.6, 3.8)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 1.1, margin = margin(b = 4)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey45", hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 1.1, margin = margin(b = 12)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, color = "grey50", hjust = 1, margin = margin(t = 10)),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap("Chart 1: NYC Airbnb Business Heavily Rely on Listings / Online Catalog", width = 65),
    subtitle = str_wrap("Statistics Regarding Market Volume, Pricing Metrics, Occupancy, and Daily Revenue", width = 60),
    caption = "Source: NYC Airbnb listings data"
  )
```

Chart 1: Illustrates the foundational market baseline for NYC short-term rentals, anchored by a vast record of catalog of **14,253 listings**. The metrics highlight a notable financial skew where upper-tier properties pull average values above typical experiences, as the **mean price (\$201.40)** and **mean daily revenue (\$94.87)** exceed their respective medians of **\$142.00** and **\$66.70**. Simultaneously, steady property utilization is reflected by a **median occupancy rate of 58.1%** (and a mean of 51.8%), demonstrating how cumulative catalog volume and consistent demand sustain the local market.

```{r Chart 2, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| fig-align: center
# 2. Data transformation and filtering to cap prices consistently at $2,500
listings_filtered <- listings %>%
  mutate(
    daily_revenue = price * occupancy,
    occupancy_pct = occupancy * 100,
    host_is_superhost_label = ifelse(host_is_superhost %in% c(TRUE, "t", "TRUE"), "Superhost", "Non-Superhost")
  ) %>%
  filter(price > 0 & price <= 2500)

# 3. Faceted price distribution chart optimized for portrait PDF view
ggplot(listings_filtered, aes(x = price, fill = host_is_superhost_label)) +
  # Draw histograms for each host category
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, color = "white", alpha = 0.85, show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Direct bar count labels on top of each bin
  stat_bin(
    bins = 15,
    geom = "text",
    aes(label = after_stat(count)),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 3.3,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "gray20"
  ) +
  # Separate sub-plots by Host Status for maximum legibility
  facet_wrap(~ host_is_superhost_label, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  # Log-scale X axis explicitly capped at 2500 with clean whole-dollar labels
  scale_x_log10(
    limits = c(NA, 2500),
    breaks = c(10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2500),
    labels = scales::dollar_format(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  # Professional color palette
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Superhost" = "#2b5c8f", "Non-Superhost" = "#e07a5f")) +
  # Expand upper Y limits so count numbers don't clip at the top margin
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  # Theme customization for margins, centered wrapped headers, and clean X-axis labels
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 1.1),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40", margin = margin(b = 15), lineheight = 1.1),
    # Reduced font size and refined positioning to prevent X-axis crowding
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 8.5),
    # Adds ample padding around the plot to prevent text clipping at the fringes
    plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 15, l = 20, unit = "pt")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap("Chart 2: From Spare Rooms to Institutional Portfolios: Host status splits the NYC Airbnb Price comparison", width = 65),
    subtitle = str_wrap("Comparison of Superhost & Non Superhost: Log-scale price distribution: Comparing Superhosts and Non-Superhosts", width = 60),
    x = "Price per Night",
    y = "Number of Listings",
    caption = "Source: NYC Airbnb listings data"
  )
```

Chart 2: Compares the log-scale price distributions of NYC Airbnb listings between Non-Superhosts and Superhosts. Both host categories concentrate their listings heavily in the \$100 to \$250 price range, while Non-Superhosts maintain a significantly higher total volume of listings across the board.

```{r Chart 3 Borough Level Performance, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center



# 1. Compute borough summary statistics
borough_summary <- listings %>%
  group_by(neighbourhood_group) %>%
  summarise(
    Listings = n(),
    Mean_Price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Occupancy = mean(occupancy_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Revenue = mean(daily_revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Revenue = median(daily_revenue, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(neighbourhood_group = reorder(neighbourhood_group, Mean_Revenue))

min_rev_borough <- borough_summary %>% filter(Mean_Revenue == min(Mean_Revenue)) %>% pull(neighbourhood_group)

# 2. Panel A: Revenue Comparison (Showing legend ONLY for Dark Blue vs Coral/Brown)
rev_long <- borough_summary %>%
  select(neighbourhood_group, Mean_Revenue, Median_Revenue) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Mean_Revenue, Median_Revenue), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Revenue") %>%
  mutate(
    Metric = if_else(Metric == "Mean_Revenue", "Mean Revenue", "Median Revenue"),
    Is_Lowest = neighbourhood_group == min_rev_borough
  )

p_rev <- ggplot(rev_long, aes(x = Revenue, y = neighbourhood_group, fill = interaction(Metric, Is_Lowest))) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = dollar(Revenue)), position = position_dodge(0.6), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c(
      "Mean Revenue.FALSE" = "#2b5c8f", 
      "Median Revenue.FALSE" = "#e07a5f",
      "Mean Revenue.TRUE" = "#e63946", 
      "Median Revenue.TRUE" = "#d62828"
    ),
    breaks = c("Mean Revenue.FALSE", "Median Revenue.FALSE"),
    labels = c("Mean Revenue", "Median Revenue")
  ) +
  labs(title = "Daily Revenue", x = "Revenue ($)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.margin = margin(t = 5)
  )

# 3. Panel B: Mean Price (Legend hidden)
p_price <- ggplot(borough_summary, aes(x = Mean_Price, y = neighbourhood_group)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = Mean_Price == min(Mean_Price)), width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = dollar(Mean_Price)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#81b29a", "TRUE" = "#e63946")) +
  labs(title = "Mean Price", x = "Price ($)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

# 4. Panel C: Mean Occupancy (Legend hidden)
p_occ <- ggplot(borough_summary, aes(x = Mean_Occupancy, y = neighbourhood_group)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = Mean_Occupancy == min(Mean_Occupancy)), width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(Mean_Occupancy / 100, accuracy = 0.1)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#f4a261", "TRUE" = "#e63946")) +
  labs(title = "Mean Occupancy", x = "Occupancy (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

# 5. Panel D: Listing Volume (Legend hidden)
p_list <- ggplot(borough_summary, aes(x = Listings, y = neighbourhood_group)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = Listings == min(Listings)), width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(Listings)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#9d4edd", "TRUE" = "#e63946")) +
  labs(title = "Listing Volume", x = "Listings", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

# 6. Combine all panels side-by-side cleanly
final_borough_chart <- (p_rev | p_price | p_occ | p_list) + 
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Chart 3: Identifying which area is low performing in NYC Airbnb",
    subtitle = "Red bars highlight the lowest performing borough across Revenue, Price, Occupancy, and Volume",
    caption = "Source: NYC Airbnb listings data",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "grey40")
    )
  )

print(final_borough_chart)
```

Chart 3: Breaks down NYC Airbnb performance by borough across daily revenue, mean price, occupancy rate, and listing volume, with red bars marking the lowest performers. **Manhattan** and **Brooklyn** lead the market in volume, pricing, and revenue, whereas the **Bronx** lags behind with the lowest figures in mean price (\$119.05) and occupancy (41.1%), and **Staten Island** records the lowest inventory with just 248 listings.

The chart also shows that volume is not directly proportion with the Daily Revenue mean price and mean occupancy.

From the chart, question arises that what are the challenges or factors that play into these lower stats in Bronx (**mean price and mean occupancy**) and **listing volumes** in Staten Island.

Chart 4: The core takeaway from Chart 4 ties directly back to the borough-level trends seen in Chart 3:

- **Entire Home/Apt Lag:** In Chart 4, **Entire home/apt** listings in the Bronx generate a median daily revenue of **\$42.10**, making them the lowest-earning entire-home listings across all five NYC boroughs.

- **Private & Shared Room Shortfalls:** The Bronx's **Private room** (\$28.70) and **Shared room** (\$21.80) earnings rank as the **2nd lowest** in their respective room categories across New York City.

- **Cumulative Market Impact:** Combined with its borough-wide baseline in Chart 3, where the Bronx records the city's **lowest mean price (\$119.05)** and **lowest mean occupancy (41.1%)**; these room-level deficits confirm that the Bronx is overall the lowest earning-yielding market in the NYC Airbnb ecosystem

```{r Chart 5.0, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center
df_summary <- listings %>%
  mutate(
    occupancy_pct = occupancy * 100,
    shared_bath_pct = as.numeric(bathrooms_shared) * 100
  ) %>%
  group_by(borough) %>%
  summarise(
    Occupancy_Rate = mean(occupancy_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    Location_Rating = mean(review_scores_location, na.rm = TRUE),
    Shared_Bathrooms = mean(shared_bath_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    Booking_Velocity = mean(reviews_per_month, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # Reverse factor levels so the Bronx appears at the top when plotted horizontally
  mutate(borough = factor(borough, levels = c("Staten Island", "Queens", "Manhattan", "Brooklyn", "Bronx")))

# 2. Reshape to long format and generate custom formatted text labels per metric
df_long <- df_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -borough,
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Metric = gsub("_", " ", Metric),
    label_text = case_when(
      Metric == "Occupancy Rate" ~ sprintf("%.1f%%", Value),
      Metric == "Location Rating" ~ sprintf("%.2f", Value),
      Metric == "Shared Bathrooms" ~ sprintf("%.1f%%", Value),
      Metric == "Booking Velocity" ~ sprintf("%.2f", Value)
    )
  )

# 3. Define color palette (Bronx highlighted in orange, others in blue)
borough_colors <- c(
  "Bronx" = "#d95f02", 
  "Brooklyn" = "#4575b4", 
  "Manhattan" = "#4575b4", 
  "Queens" = "#4575b4", 
  "Staten Island" = "#4575b4"
)

# 4. Create Faceted Horizontal Lollipop Chart in an even 2x2 grid
p <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = Value, y = borough, color = borough)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = Value, y = borough, yend = borough), linewidth = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label_text), hjust = -0.25, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = borough_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) + # Adds breathing room on the right for text labels
  facet_wrap(~ Metric, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) + # 2 columns creates an even 2x2 panel layout
  labs(
    title = str_wrap("Chart 5: Challenges faced by the listings in Bronx vs other Borough", width=60),
    subtitle = str_wrap("Comparing occupancy, ratings, shared amenities, and booking velocity", width=50),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 11, margin = margin(b = 15), hjust = 0.5),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10)
  )

# Display and save
print(p)
ggsave("borough_lollipop_dashboard_labeled.png", p, width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

The Bronx faces severe structural disadvantages across all key short-term rental performance metrics compared to the rest of New York City. It records the lowest occupancy rate in the city at **41.1%**, the slowest booking velocity at **1.11 reviews per month**, the lowest location rating at **4.57 out of 5**, and the cheapest average listing price at **\$119.05**. Compounding these low demand and pricing figures, the Bronx also suffers from the highest proportion of shared bathrooms at **39.4%**, highlighting a lower-tier infrastructure that struggles to compete with more lucrative and fully equipped markets like Manhattan and Brooklyn.

```{r Chart 6, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  labs(
    title = str_wrap("Chart 6: Capitalizing on the Bronx Advantage: Quality and Engagement Metrics", width = 65),
    subtitle = str_wrap("Evaluating top-tier rating quality, value perception, and review volumes across NYC boroughs.", width = 60),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 6)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 11, margin = margin(b = 20), hjust = 0.5),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, color = "#1e293b"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#e2e8f0", linewidth = 0.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "#334155"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, color = "#64748b"),
    plot.margin = margin(20, 20, 20, 20)
  )

# Display and save
print(p)
```

Chart 6 evaluates key quality and engagement metrics across New York City boroughs, highlighting the Bronx's strong foundation in guest satisfaction alongside opportunities for volume growth. The borough achieves competitive guest ratings with a mean rating of 4.71 and a value score of 4.65, closely matching core markets like Manhattan and Brooklyn. Although total review counts are lower—averaging 38.9 reviews—these consistent, top-tier quality scores demonstrate that Bronx listings maintain an excellent guest experience ready for strategic positioning and marketing.

```{r Chart_8_Resolution_Roadmap, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| fig-align: center

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Chart 8A: Infrastructure Bottleneck (Shared Bathrooms vs. Occupancy Rate)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
df_friction <- data.frame(
  borough = factor(c("Bronx", "Queens", "Brooklyn", "Manhattan"), levels = c("Bronx", "Queens", "Brooklyn", "Manhattan")),
  shared_bath_pct = c(39.4, 36.2, 28.4, 18.2),
  occupancy_pct = c(41.1, 44.5, 52.2, 56.8)
) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(shared_bath_pct, occupancy_pct), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value") %>%
  mutate(
    Metric_Label = if_else(Metric == "shared_bath_pct", "Shared Bathrooms (%)", "Occupancy Rate (%)")
  )

p7a <- ggplot(df_friction, aes(x = borough, y = Value, fill = interaction(Metric, borough == "Bronx"))) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", Value)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#1e293b"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "shared_bath_pct.TRUE"  = "#e11d48", # Highlight Bronx Shared Bathrooms in Red/Rose
      "occupancy_pct.TRUE"    = "#f59e0b", # Highlight Bronx Occupancy in Amber
      "shared_bath_pct.FALSE" = "#cbd5e1", # Muted slate grey for benchmarks
      "occupancy_pct.FALSE"   = "#94a3b8"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18)), labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "7A. The Infrastructure Bottleneck",
    subtitle = "Shared bathroom prevalence directly correlates with lower occupancy across boroughs.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percentage (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, color = "#0f172a"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 10, margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "#1e293b")
  )

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Chart 8B: Actionable Intervention Roadmap (Revenue Uplift Potential)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
df_action <- data.frame(
  Action = factor(
    c(
      "Private Bath Conversion\n(CapEx Upgrade)",
      "Amenity Positioning\n(Highlight 37+ Amenities)",
      "Dynamic Pricing\n(Capture Peak Demand)",
      "Transit & Location\nTransparency"
    ),
    levels = rev(c(
      "Private Bath Conversion\n(CapEx Upgrade)",
      "Dynamic Pricing\n(Capture Peak Demand)",
      "Amenity Positioning\n(Highlight 37+ Amenities)",
      "Transit & Location\nTransparency"
    ))
  ),
  Uplift = c(35, 22, 18, 15)
)

p7b <- ggplot(df_action, aes(x = Uplift, y = Action)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1b9e77", width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("+%d%% Uplift", Uplift)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#0f172a"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25)), labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "7B. Strategic Action & Revenue Uplift Roadmap",
    subtitle = "Estimated revenue expansion potential per Bronx listing upon operational remedy.",
    x = "Estimated Revenue Uplift Potential (%)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, color = "#0f172a"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 10, margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5, color = "#1e293b")
  )

# Combine both panels using patchwork
chart_7_combined <- (p7a + p7b) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Chart 8: Strategic Resolution Roadmap for Bronx STR Optimization",
    subtitle = "From Infrastructure Remedy to Revenue Maximization: Converting Structural Challenges into High-Yield Investment.",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0.5, color = "#0f172a"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 11, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15))
    )
  )

print(chart_7_combined)
```

## Strategic Resolution & Remedy Summary

**Strategic Pricing & Yield Management**

1.  Move beyond the discounting trap: Hold baseline price floors near \$119.05 while utilizing dynamic pricing for peak seasons.

2.  Leverage Quality: Use high review accuracy (4.71) to support optimal rate adjustments but without sacrificung perceived quality.

**Targeted CapEx & Infrastructure Upgrades**

1.  Upgrade Bathrooms: Convert shared bathrooms (39.4%) to private en-suites to overcome the occupancy lag.

2.  Showcase Amenities in the listings: Prominently feature the borough's high average amenity count (37.4) to drive bookings.

**Positioning & Marketing Optimization**

1.  Highlight Space: Market entire-home listings based on square-foot value relative to cramped Manhattan units.

2.  Ensure Transparency: Proactively highlight transit links upfront to offset lower location ratings (4.57).

**Investor Acquisition & Portfolio Strategy**

1.  Low Acquisition Cost, High ROI Potential: Capitalize on lower acquisition prices in the Bronx to achieve superior cap rates.

2.  Focus on Entire Homes inventory: Prioritize entire-home inventory to maximize revenue potential.
